candidate_relations.reason: The histopathology and immunohistochemistry (S100 positive, GFAP patchy positive, CD34 negative) are consistent with myxoma, not schwannoma. While S100 can be positive in schwannoma, the overall cellularity, myxoid stroma, and lack of other schwannoma features rule it out.

The candidate 'Myxoma of the ciliary body' is a complete equivalent to the reference 'Ciliary body myxoma'. The clinical presentation, imaging (ultrasound biomicroscopy showing a cystoid mass with a stalk attached to the pars plana), and especially the histopathological findings (hypovascular myxoid lesion, loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells, hypocellular core with abundant myxoid stroma, no epithelial components, mitoses, or atypical cells) along with immunohistochemistry (S100 positive, GFAP patchy positive, CD34 negative) are all highly characteristic of a ciliary body myxoma.

While GFAP is patchy positive, the overall histopathology (myxoid stroma, spindle/stellate cells, S100 positivity) is not consistent with a glial choristoma, which would typically show mature glial tissue.

Medulloepithelioma is an embryonal tumor with epithelial and neuroectodermal components, often showing mitotic activity and atypical cells. The histopathology described (hypovascular myxoid lesion, no epithelial components, no mitoses, no atypical cells) directly contradicts a diagnosis of medulloepithelioma.
